propositions: The review-bot service must be reconfigured to use Bedrock inference profiles instead of direct Anthropic API, with separate model classes for frontier (opus), standard (sonnet), and trivial (haiku) passes to dogfood the client pathway.

The Docker image must include the bedrock extra for pydantic-ai-slim so the provider module is available at runtime; the current image lacks it despite having boto3 present, which would cause silent failures on first Bedrock call.

A CloudWatch alarm dimensioned by ModelId must monitor Bedrock InvokeModel client-error rates with a 25% threshold over 15-minute windows, providing visibility into partial degradation that the existing voter-error alarm cannot detect.

The production cutover cannot proceed until safety infrastructure is proven: the voter-error alarm must transition OK→ALARM on an induced failure while the bot is still on Anthropic, and the Bedrock import must resolve inside the running container.

The kill switch must be executable post-cutover by deleting the three environment variable overrides, reverting to built-in anthropic:claude-* defaults, with the Anthropic credential retained by design to support recovery without requiring secrets re-provisioning.

Post-cutover verification must confirm via REBAR_USAGE_LOG that all LLM calls reach Bedrock inference profiles (not direct Anthropic), the per-pass model split is preserved (opus for frontier, sonnet for standard/verify/coach), and caching engages successfully.
